file.notApplied: The settings file is not applied: the last good version stays until it is fixed

sla.hours: {{queue}} works {{hours}} ({{zone}}); the clock stops outside them and while waiting on the customer.
sla.always: {{queue}} works round the clock; the clock stops only while waiting on the customer.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: Every queue, now and the last 30 days. SLA clocks run in each queue's working hours and pause while waiting on the customer.
overview.perDayDetail: Opened and solved, the last 30 days
overview.perDayLabel: Tickets opened and solved per day
overview.atRiskDetail: Under an hour left, or missed
overview.noneAtRisk: No SLA runs out within the hour.

queue.title: Queues
queue.description: Open tickets with their SLAs. A ticket goes to the first queue whose rule in the settings file matches its address, form or customer.
queue.subject: Subject

ticket.solvedNotice: {{number}} solved. {{name}} is asked how it went.
ticket.movedNotice: Moved to {{queue}}; its SLA starts for the clocks not met or missed.
ticket.cannotReply: Replies cannot be sent from here
ticket.noEmail: This ticket has no customer email. Add internal notes, or answer where the customer wrote.
ticket.noSmtp: {{address}} has no SMTP server in the settings file.
ticket.sent: Reply sent to {{to}} from {{from}}. The SLA clock pauses until {{name}} answers.
ticket.sentSolved: Reply sent to {{to}} from {{from}}, and the ticket is solved.
ticket.queued: The reply is in the outbox and is tried again: {{error}}
ticket.routed: Queue {{queue}}, set by the rule {{rule}} in the settings file. Moving it to another queue starts that queue's SLA.
ticket.notSentYet: The reply is not sent yet

event.opened: Opened from {{from}}. Routed to {{queue}} by the rule {{rule}}.
event.openedSla: Opened from {{from}}. Routed to {{queue}} by the rule {{rule}}; SLA {{sla}}.
event.crmUnavailable: CRM did not answer, so the customer's plan was not used for routing.
event.reopened: Reopened: the customer answered after it was solved.
event.waiting: Waiting on the customer, set by {{name}}.
event.bounce: An email to {{recipients}} could not be delivered.
event.deliveryFailed: An email could not be sent: {{error}}

customer.title: Customer
customer.notFound: No CRM contact has the address {{email}}.
customer.noEmail: This ticket has no customer email.

reports.title: Reports
reports.description: The last {{days}} days, by queue. Times count in each queue's working hours.
reports.arriveDetail: Average a week, by weekday and hour ({{zone}})
reports.busiest: {{share}}% of tickets arrive on {{day}} between {{from}}:00 and {{to}}:00.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: Where tickets come from and what each ticket shows beside it. Each is set in the settings file.
integrations.emailDetail: Read over IMAP and answered over SMTP, from any mail server; addresses on OpenAsy Mail work the same way.
integrations.noAddresses: No addresses in the settings file: tickets come from forms and chats only.
integrations.outbox: Outbox: {{queued}} waiting to be sent, {{failed}} failed in 7 days.
integrations.ignoredDetail: Auto-replies, bounces, lists and loops, the last 30 days
integrations.formsDetail: POST /api/v1/public/tickets with a source's key from a server, or from a page on its origins.
integrations.htmlForm: A plain HTML form on {{origins}} works without a key:
integrations.noSources: No sources in the settings file.
integrations.crmOn: Linked to {{url}}: the customer and their deals beside each ticket, matched by email only.
integrations.crmOff: Not linked: nothing from CRM is shown. Add crm to the settings file; Helpdesk asks it like this.
integrations.kbOn: Linked to {{url}}: articles are suggested beside the reply box.
integrations.kbOff: Not linked: no articles are suggested. Add knowledge_base to the settings file.
integrations.apiDetail: Every screen uses the same API, with a session or an API token.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Queues, routing rules, SLAs and the links to other products, as {{file}} sets them.
settings.readOnlyDetail: Change them in the file and review the change like code; Helpdesk reads it again within a minute. A file with a mistake leaves the last good version in place.
settings.noFile: No settings file: the defaults are in use.
settings.notApplied: The file on disk is not applied
settings.queuesDetail: A ticket goes to the first queue whose rule matches.
settings.name: Name

token.subject: In the subject, [#1001]
token.both: In the subject and the reply address

auth.accountDetail: Your name, password and second factors.
auth.membersDetail: Who works in Helpdesk, and their role: viewers read, editors answer tickets, admins also manage members and tokens.
auth.signinDetail: How people sign in: passwords, and identity providers over OIDC.
auth.tokensDetail: Tokens for scripts and other products, each with one role and an expiry.
auth.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Helpdesk.
